daily_report_items: RTX is a medium-confidence baseline near miss: backlog, segment growth, cash generation, and liquidity are strengths, but engine remediation, leverage, contract execution, valuation, overbought timing, and the absent accepted relationship remain material; the USD 218.42 mark exceeds the USD 142.00 downside and USD 179.38 base scenario values.

evidence.claim: RTX reported Q2 2026 sales of USD 24.7 billion, GAAP EPS of USD 1.57, operating cash flow of USD 3.5 billion, USD 289 billion of backlog, and adjusted 2026 EPS guidance of USD 7.10-7.25. The issuer release returned HTTP 200.

The filed Q2 2026 report shows USD 8.305 billion of cash, USD 37.383 billion of total debt, USD 63.912 billion of current assets, USD 63.245 billion of current liabilities, first-half operating cash flow of USD 5.402 billion, and continuing Pratt powder-metal uncertainty. The filing returned HTTP 200.
evidence.source: RTX Corporation Q2 2026 Form 10-Q filed with the SEC

evidence.claim: RTX closed at USD 218.4199981689453 on 2026-07-27 and the current USD/EUR rate was 0.8794000148773193. Applying 20 times the USD 7.10 guidance low gives USD 142.00 and -35.0%; applying 25 times the USD 7.175 midpoint gives USD 179.375 and -17.9%.
evidence.source: PaperTrader deterministic market and FX caches

summary: Revalidated RTX against its SEC-filed Q2 2026 Form 10-Q, issuer results, and current 2026-07-27 market and FX data. Backlog, segment growth, cash generation, and liquidity support medium-confidence baseline eligibility, while Pratt engine remediation, leverage, contract execution, cycle sensitivity, valuation, and timing remain material gaps. At the USD 218.42 mark, bounded 12-month earnings scenarios imply 35.0% downside and 17.9% base-case downside. No conviction strategy follow-up was enqueued because both scenario values remain below the mark and no accepted idea-to-security relationship exists.
